_comment: The parameter set the throughput measurement was taken with, kept separate from
params.example.json because it is not the default shape and costs materially more.
Four values differ from params.example.json, and each one is load-bearing:
HostInstanceType    c5n.9xlarge, not t3.small. c5n.9xlarge is the smallest c5n whose
published network figure is a flat 50 Gbps rather than 'Up to 25',
which is what allows the client to be ruled out as the bottleneck.
$2.448/h against $0.272/h for c5n.xlarge (ap-northeast-1, on-demand
Linux, effective 2026-08-01). Keep the runs short.
OriginVolumeSizeMB  204800 (200 GiB), not 10240. A single 30-second write point at the
2048 MBps step lands about 61 GB. The measurement script deletes
after every point for this reason, but one point still has to fit.
AssociatePublicIp   true only where the subnet has neither a NAT gateway nor SSM
interface endpoints. A host with no route to the SSM endpoints comes
up healthy and is simply absent from Session Manager.
HostS3DataAccess    true, so the host can drive the S3 API sweep itself. This is the one
that widens the blast radius: narrow HostS3ResourceArns to the two
target ARNs once they exist, especially in a shared account.
ThroughputCapacityMBps stays at 128 here. That is the step the visibility records were
taken on, so it is the step that compares with them. Raise it afterwards with
`aws fsx update-file-system` and re-run: the update is online and took 24 minutes, and
2048 MBps costs about $2.58/h while it is held.
Copy to params.throughput.json, replace the two network placeholders, and delete this
_comment key.
